chunks: Al-Rida عليه السلام said: “Regarding the two sajdahs of forgetfulness: if you made a deficiency, then before the taslim; and if you made an addition, then after it.”
(770) 71. And what was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Sinan, from Abi al-Jarud, who said:

I said to Abi Ja‘far عليه السلام: “When should I perform the two sajdahs of forgetfulness?” He said: “Before the taslim, for if you give the taslim and then do it afterward, the sanctity of your salat has departed.”

These two reports are to be understood as pertaining to a type of taqiyyah, because they accord with the doctrines of the generality. And Abu Ja‘far Muhammad ibn ‘Ali ibn Babawayh, may Allah have mercy on him, said: “I give legal ruling by them in the state of taqiyyah.”

(771) 72. As for what was narrated by Sa‘d ibn ‘Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn ‘Ali ibn Faddal, from ‘Amr ibn Sa‘id al-Mada’ini, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from ‘Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati, from Abi ‘Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about the two sajdahs of forgetfulness: “Is there takbir or tasbih in them?” He said: “No, they are only two sajdahs. If the one who forgot is the Imam, he says takbir when he prostrates and when he raises his head, so as to inform those behind him that he has forgotten. And there is no obligation upon him to recite tasbih in them, nor is there in them a tashahhud after the two sajdahs.”

What is meant by this report is that there is not in them tasbih and tashahhud like the tasbih and tashahhud in the salats in terms of lengthening them, not that what is meant is the negation of tasbih and tashahhud in every respect. According to us, what is prescribed is that a person should keep brief the tashahhud after the two sajdahs of forgetfulness, praise Allah, the Exalted, during the prostration, and send blessings upon His Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله with no prolongation. And that which clarifies what we have mentioned...

ai.seo_question: When are the two sajdahs of forgetfulness performed, and what is recited in them according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This passage discusses the rulings of sajdatay al-sahw in salat, including whether they are performed before or after the taslim and what is recited in them. It also records a juristic reconciliation of reports, including that some narrations are understood as issued under taqiyyah and that the prescribed practice is brief dhikr and tashahhud without prolongation.
